description: This line plot illustrates the average correct gate rate across 31 embedding layers (from layer 0 to layer 30) for four different input configurations in a Llama model: Character Attention input (solid blue), Character MLP input (dashed blue), Wiki Attention input (solid red), and Wiki MLP input (dashed red). The x-axis, labeled “Embedding Layer,” is linear and spans from 0 to 30, with major gridlines at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Average Correct Gate Rate,” is linear and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.2. Each line is accompanied by a shaded region representing the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. The Character MLP input (dashed blue) and Wiki MLP input (dashed red) consistently outperform their attention counterparts across most layers, with both MLP lines generally staying above 0.8 after layer 15. The Character Attention input (solid blue) peaks near layer 5 at approximately 0.81 before declining sharply to around 0.25 at layer 12, then recovering to about 0.75 by layer 30. The Wiki Attention input (solid red) starts at 0.2, rises steeply to 0.8 at layer 5, drops to 0.38 at layer 13, and then gradually increases to 0.7 by layer 30. The MLP inputs show more stable and higher performance, especially beyond layer 15, supporting the paper’s conclusion that MLP layer inputs yield better embeddings for gating.
